author: Traditional, as sung in the mead halls

#Song of the Long Hearth

~Bank up the fire, the night is long,
~the wind is at the door;
~we'll warm our hands and raise a song
~as our fathers did before.

~The snow lies deep upon the pass,
~the wolves are on the hill,
~but here the mead is in the glass
~and the hearth is burning still.

~We'll sing of those who crossed the sea
~in boats of oak and hide,
~who found this land of stone and tree
~and made their hearths inside.

~We'll sing of those who went to war
~and those who stayed to plough,
~and those who will come home no more:
~we keep their places now.

~So bank the fire and fill the horn,
~and let the old songs ring,
~for every winter night is torn
~by morning and by spring.

~And when my own long night shall fall
~and I am laid to rest,
~remember me within this hall,
~where the hearth burned brightest.
